findings.claim: DESIGN.md §4.1's schema listing (line 300) orders `runs` columns as `(run_id, batch_id, repo_id, base_sha, ...)`, but this diff places `batch_id` after `repo_id` instead. Harmless since every reader in this module uses `sqlite3.Row` name-based access (verified: no positional row access on `runs` exists anywhere in `saffron/`), so this is purely a textual mismatch with the cited design section, not a functional one.

No test calls `create_run` with a real (non-`None`) `batch_id` and checks it round-trips into `runs.batch_id` — every new test exercises only the omitted-argument path. Replacing `batch_id` with a hard-coded `None` in the INSERT tuple (leaving the parameter accepted but discarded) keeps all 1250 tests, the `revert` gate, and `census` green, because the only assertions made are `row['batch_id'] is None` after calling `create_run` with no `batch_id` argument at all. The acceptance criterion this line serves ('runs carries a nullable batch_id') is verified only for the trivial NULL case; the mechanism that will actually link a run to a batch in `SA-0049` has no witness here.

probe.find:
cursor = self._db.execute(
            """INSERT INTO runs (repo_id, base_sha, batch_id, status)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'RUNNING')""",
            (repo_id, base_sha, batch_id),
        )
probe.replace:
cursor = self._db.execute(
            """INSERT INTO runs (repo_id, base_sha, batch_id, status)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'RUNNING')""",
            (repo_id, base_sha, None),
        )
